title: Knowing and Seeing: Talks and Questions & Answers at a Meditation Retreat in Taiwan
author: Pa-Auk Tawya Sayadaw
edition_cited: Fourth Revised Edition, Pa-Auk Meditation Centre, Singapore, 2010 (archive.org text of the free-distribution PDF)
locator_hints: Talk 1, 'How You Develop Mindfulness-of-Breathing': four stages, each tried 'for about one hour' before moving on if no nimitta appears (file lines c. 2700-2900)
Talk 1, section 'THE NIMITTA' (file line 2908 ff.): light before the nimitta vs the nimitta; do not play with it; ignore a nimitta far away; when to shift from breath to nimitta; uggaha to patibhaga
Q&A 1.2-1.4 (line 4882 ff.): is a nimitta necessary; where it comes from; 'real' vs not-real nimitta
Talk 2: white kasina from the skeleton, expanding the nimitta; 'How You Develop the Light Kasina' (line 5805) and fire kasina
Introduction, 'You Develop the Light of Wisdom' (line 1486) and Q&A 4.10 (line 11872) on the light experienced in meditation
Talk on insight: obhasa among the imperfections (search 'imperfection')
summary: Step-by-step Pa Auk instruction for bringing up the breath nimitta. Attention is held at the touch-point; four stages (long/short, whole breath, tranquillising) are each worked for about an hour and the meditator moves on if no nimitta appears. The text distinguishes a preliminary light from the nimitta proper ('as the sun is different from sunlight'), lists the forms it takes (cotton wool, morning star, ruby, pearl and others), and gives handling rules: do not play with it or shift to it early, ignore one that appears far in front, move to it only when it is stable at the touch-point and merged with the breath; hold the white uggaha-nimitta for one to three hours until it turns bright as the patibhaga-nimitta. Later talks give the white, fire and light kasinas, expansion of the sign, and the 'light of concentration' used as a working light for discerning body parts and beings; Q&A explains what the light is.
why_relevant: Explicit induction and development procedure for a seen closed-eye light, with troubleshooting for the meditator for whom nothing appears and for a nimitta that is unstable or misplaced.
